title: InfScaler: Enabling Efficient ML Inference Serving on Multi-Accelerator Edge Devices via Asymmetric Auto-Scaling
problem: Multi-accelerator edge SoCs with heterogeneous compute units (CPU, GPU, NPU, TPU) are poorly utilized by existing inference frameworks that lack bottleneck awareness and cannot efficiently partition models across diverse accelerators.
motivation: Edge ML deployment is growing; maximizing throughput and minimizing resource waste on heterogeneous SoCs is critical for battery life and latency-sensitive applications.
method: Discovers architectural bottleneck of ML models through profiling, designs bottleneck-aware asymmetric auto-scaling to allocate resources unequally to different model stages, leverages unified memory in edge SoCs for efficient data sharing between asymmetrically scaled partitions.
key_novelty: Bottleneck-aware asymmetric auto-scaling technique that unequally allocates resources across accelerators and leverages SoC unified memory for efficient multi-partition inference.
contributions: Architectural bottleneck discovery framework for ML models on edge SoCs
Asymmetric auto-scaling for efficient heterogeneous resource allocation
Unified memory optimization for data sharing between scaled model partitions
126.59% throughput improvement with 27.32% resource reduction vs. state-of-the-art
limitations: Limited to models fitting within unified memory; large-scale model partitioning across remote devices not discussed.
primary_theme: Bottleneck-aware asymmetric auto-scaling for multi-accelerator edge ML inference
